A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete Appendices A–E. Pages 2–33 have identical extracted text and rendered content; page 1 differs only in abstract wording and date/version text.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical regret guarantees, and proofs. Neither the main text nor Appendices A–E report original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the same theoretical material. No original empirical outcomes appear in its main text or Appendices A–E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the least-squares objectives, uncertainty filtering, confidence sets, and variance-estimation procedures in Sections 3–5 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation scenarios. Both study the same theoretical contextual-bandit setting.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated baselines. The theoretical discussions of Optimistic Least Squares, SquareCB, and SAVE are unchanged.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol, data split, training budget, or testing procedure.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies appear in either version. Appendices A–E retain the same supporting mathematical results and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. The theoretical variance estimators and probabilistic confidence guarantees are unchanged.

E6.justification: No numerical results or qualitative findings are added, removed, or revised. Both versions retain identical theoretical regret guarantees and contain no empirical performance results.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, definitions, propositions, regret bounds, and proofs are identical, including all material in Appendices A–E.

C1.justification: Both versions claim second-order regret bounds for contextual bandits with function approximation and unknown variances under mean-reward realizability. The abstract copyedit does not alter this claim or its scope.

C2.justification: The discussion of potentially non-sharp eluder-dimension dependence for changing variances remains unchanged, as do Section 6's proposed extensions to reinforcement learning and inverse-gap-weighting methods.

D1.justification: Algorithm specifications and technical details are identical. Neither version adds implementation instructions, hardware information, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and research-positioning passages are retained, including comparisons with prior work requiring known variances or distributional realizability.

P1.justification: The abstract corrects 'algorithms no-regret algorithms' to 'no-regret algorithms' and replaces 'mean rewards' with 'mean reward function.' The first-page date and arXiv version text are updated; document structure and remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The page layout and Algorithm 1–3 displays are retained, with no added, removed, or redesigned figures or tables. The abstract copyedit causes only incidental line wrapping.

improvement.justification: v2 removes duplicated wording and improves grammatical precision in the abstract's opening sentence. This is a small editorial improvement; the scientific claims, algorithms, theoretical guarantees, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged.
